content: 1. Yeboah-Manu D and colleagues conducted a study on the co-infection of Buruli ulcer and HIV in the Ga district of Ghana, which was presented at the World Health Organization (WHO) meeting on Buruli ulcer control and research in Geneva, Switzerland, in 2013. 2. Christine V and colleagues investigated the impact of HIV on the severity of Buruli ulcer disease through a retrospective study conducted in Cameroon, with their findings published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2014. 3. Kibadi K and colleagues reported on Buruli ulcer lesions in HIV-positive patients, with their findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 16, Pages 738–739). 4. Johnson RC and colleagues presented a case study on disseminated Mycobacterium ulcerans disease in an HIV-positive patient, published in AIDS in 2002 (Volume 16, Pages 1704–1705). 5. Toll A and colleagues described a case of aggressive multifocal Buruli ulcer with associated osteomyelitis in an HIV-positive patient, published in Clinical and Experimental Dermatology in 2005 (Volume 30, Pages 649–651). 6. The World Health Organization published consolidated guidelines in 2013 on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing recommendations for a public health approach. 7. The World Health Organization also released guidelines in 2010 on antiretroviral therapy for HIV infection in adults and adolescents. 8. Kuper JI and D’Aprile M explored clinically significant drug-drug interactions in the treatment of patients with Mycobacterium avium complex disease. 9. Wallace R and colleagues reported reduced serum levels of clarithromycin in patients treated with multidrug regimens that included rifampin or rifabutin for Mycobacterium avium–M. intracellulare infection, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1997 (Volume 171, Pages 747–750). 10. The product information for Sustiva, an antiretroviral medication, was published by Bristol-Myers Squibb in Princeton, NJ, in 2010. 11. Nelson MR and colleagues evaluated the safety of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for the treatment of HIV infection in adults over the first four years, with their findings published in AIDS in 2007 (Volume 21, Pages 1273–1281). 12. O’Brien DP and colleagues discussed the management of Buruli ulcer and HIV co-infection in their publication. 13. The World Health Organization published guidance in 2012 for health workers on the treatment of Mycobacterium ulcerans disease (Buruli ulcer). 14. O’Brien DP and colleagues explored the use of moxifloxacin for treating Buruli ulcer in HIV co-infected patients, questioning whether it could address both conditions simultaneously, with their findings published in AIDS in 2013 (Volume 27, Pages 2177–2179).
